title: On 5 July 2026, ICE Acting Director Todd Lyons Placed Two Immigration Officers on Administrative Leave Pending an Internal Investigation After Concluding the Officers Had Made 'Untruthful Statements' in Sworn Testimony About the Shooting of a Migrant in Minneapolis — Capping at Least Five Separate Trump-Administration Immigration Shootings Whose Initial DHS Descriptions Were Later Contradicted by Video Evidence, Per the 5 July Reuters Review — and Marking the First Time a State-Level Prosecution (Hennepin County Attorney Mary Moriarty Charging ICE Agent Castro for Firing Through a Closed Door) Has Followed a Contradicted DHS Narrative.
beat: ICE perjury probe — five-shooting pattern named by Reuters — Hennepin County charges agent Castro for firing through closed door — Noem 'attempted murder' + Miller 'would-be assassin' + DHS 'shovel and broom' four-iteration fabrication vs officer bodycam + bystander video — July 5 2026
narrative: On 5 July 2026, ICE acting director Todd Lyons placed two immigration officers on administrative leave pending an internal investigation after concluding the officers had made 'untruthful statements' in sworn testimony about the shooting of a migrant in Minneapolis. ICE's statement: 'Video evidence has revealed that sworn testimony provided by two separate officers appears to have made untruthful statements.' Lyons added that the officers 'may face termination of employment, as well as potential criminal prosecution.' On 4 July, the top federal prosecutor in Minnesota, Daniel N. Rosen, asked a judge to dismiss charges against two Venezuelan men (Aljorna and Sosa-Celis), writing that 'newly discovered evidence in this matter is materially inconsistent with the allegations.' A judge granted the dismissal-with-prejudice on 4 July; it cannot be refiled. Hennepin County Attorney Mary Moriarty charged ICE agent Castro with shooting a man in the leg; the criminal complaint alleges Castro 'fired his weapon through the front door of the residence knowing there were people who had just run inside' while standing 'alone in the front yard, under no physical threat or duress.' The DHS press release the day after the shooting contained four separate iterations of the claim that Sosa-Celis's compatriots used 'a shovel and broom handle' / 'a shovel or broom stick' / 'snow shovels and the handles of brooms' to 'beat' the federal agent. The county statement says the DHS press release contains 'dozens of false statements' and remains online. The ICE perjury probe is the latest in at least five Trump-administration immigration shootings whose initial descriptions were later contradicted by video evidence, per the 5 July Reuters review published in Straits Times and HuffPost. The cumulative pattern was named in the Reuters review: 'officials rushed to defend immigration officers without waiting for key facts to emerge.' Moriarty's statement on Castro: 'Mr. Castro is an ICE agent. But his federal badge does not make him immune from state charges for his criminal conduct in Minnesota.' Minnesota Attorney General Keith Ellison: 'Nobody is above the law, including ICE agents.' The named five-incident pattern: (1) the Minneapolis shooting of the two Venezuelan men (Castro shooting through the door; 'shovel-and-broom' fabrication), (2) the fatal Minneapolis shooting of Renee Good on 7 January (DHS called her a 'violent rioter' who 'weaponised her vehicle … an act of domestic terrorism'; cellphone video from multiple angles plus an officer's own bodycam conflicted with the claims), (3) the fatal Minneapolis shooting of Alex Pretti on 24 January (DHS described him approaching with a handgun and 'violently resisted'; half-dozen bystander videos showed Pretti holding a cellphone, not a gun; an officer's bodycam showed the gun was removed from his body before shots were fired), plus two earlier incidents cited by Reuters but not individually named.
analysis:
1. The cumulative five-incident pattern named by Reuters on 5 July is the load-bearing third-party anchor. Reuters review documents five separate incidents where the official DHS account was contradicted by video evidence. The pattern formulation in Reuters: 'officials rushed to defend immigration officers without waiting for key facts to emerge.' The five-incident count converts what would otherwise be three isolated incidents into a named cumulative-pattern finding. The Reuters review is the named-third-party anchor — independent of Hennepin County, independent of the federal perjury probe, independent of the named political escalations — and it is the journalistic layer that names the pattern as a pattern rather than a series of coincidences.

2. Kristi Noem's 'attempted murder of federal law enforcement' formulation is the on-record primary-source quote. 'What we saw last night in Minneapolis was an attempted murder of federal law enforcement. Our officer was ambushed and attacked.' Noem, then-DHS Secretary. The 'shovel and broom' claim appears four times in the DHS press release — three distinct phrasings of the same fabricated detail ('a shovel and broom handle' / 'a shovel or broom stick' / 'snow shovels and the handles of brooms'). The cumulative count of false statements in the DHS press release, per Hennepin County: 'dozens.' The press release has not been retracted; it remains online. The four-iteration repetition of the same fabricated detail is the structural-fingerprint signal that the statement was not a single error but a coordinated framing.

3. Hennepin County charging an ICE agent is the unprecedented escalation and the load-bearing legal-mechanism layer. Castro was charged with shooting a man in the leg through a closed door while standing alone in the front yard. Moriarty's statement: 'Mr. Castro is an ICE agent. But his federal badge does not make him immune from state charges for his criminal conduct in Minnesota.' Minnesota Attorney General Keith Ellison: 'Nobody is above the law, including ICE agents.' This is the first time in the five-incident pattern that state-level criminal charges have followed a contradicted DHS narrative; the prior four relied on bystander video contradicting DHS without prosecution. The state-level prosecution converts the narrative-contradiction pattern into a specific legal consequence with a named charging document.

4. The cell-phone video from the officer who shot Renee Good is the asymmetric-transparency anchor. DHS described Good as a 'violent rioter' who 'weaponised her vehicle, attempting to run over our law enforcement officers … an act of domestic terrorism.' The officer's own bodycam and multiple bystander videos showed Good at the wheel of her parked SUV, telling an officer 'I'm not mad at you,' then the officer grabbed at the driver's-side door, and the SUV pulled forward while the officer fired. DHS's claim that Good 'attempted to run over' ICE officers is contradicted by her own bodycam. Reuters verification explicitly states: 'Videos of the shooting taken from several vantage points — including cellphone video recorded by the officer who shot Good — conflicted with those claims.' DHS has not retracted the original statement; it remains online.

5. Stephen Miller's 'would-be assassin' + Greg Bovino's 'massacre law enforcement' framing is the named on-record political escalation. Bovino, Border Patrol senior official: Pretti intended to 'massacre law enforcement.' Miller, Deputy White House chief of staff: 'a would-be assassin.' Both statements are on-record, both are contradicted by half-a-dozen bystander videos, both have not been retracted. Bovino has since been 'excused from his duties' as the operation leader per the 5 July Reuters review — a personnel consequence without a retraction of the statements themselves. The statements remain on the public record; the personnel removal does not walk back the original characterizations.

6. The federal perjury probe is the legal mechanism naming the pattern as 'untruthful statements.' ICE acting director Lyons: 'Video evidence has revealed that sworn testimony provided by two separate officers appears to have made untruthful statements.' US attorney's office actively investigating. 'Upon conclusion of the investigation, the officers may face termination of employment, as well as potential criminal prosecution.' This converts a five-incident narrative pattern into a specific federal perjury probe, with the named consequence ladder (termination → criminal prosecution). The 'untruthful statements' formulation is the federal government's own naming of the pattern — distinct from Hennepin County's 'dozens of false statements' characterization, distinct from Reuters's 'officials rushed to defend' framing.
verdict: [SIPHONED VERDICT]: On 5 July 2026, ICE acting director Todd Lyons placed two immigration officers on administrative leave pending an internal investigation after concluding the officers had made 'untruthful statements' in sworn testimony about the shooting of a migrant in Minneapolis, capping at least five separate Trump-administration immigration shootings whose initial DHS descriptions were later contradicted by video evidence per the 5 July Reuters review. The pattern Reuters named on 5 July: 'officials rushed to defend immigration officers without waiting for key facts to emerge.' Hennepin County Attorney Mary Moriarty charged ICE agent Castro with shooting a man in the leg through a closed door while 'alone in the front yard, under no physical threat or duress' — the first state-level prosecution following a contradicted DHS narrative in the five-incident pattern. The DHS press release the day after the Minneapolis shooting contained four separate iterations of the 'shovel and broom handle' / 'a shovel or broom stick' / 'snow shovels and the handles of brooms' fabrication; Hennepin County characterizes the press release as containing 'dozens of false statements,' and it remains online. Kristi Noem's 'attempted murder of federal law enforcement' formulation, Stephen Miller's 'would-be assassin' framing, and Greg Bovino's 'massacre law enforcement' characterization are the named on-record political escalations contradicted by named primary-source video evidence (officer bodycam in the Good shooting; half-dozen bystander videos in the Pretti shooting). The empirical floor: five named incidents + Reuters named-pattern formulation + Noem + Miller + Bovino on-record statements + officer bodycam + bystander video + Hennepin County 'dozens of false statements' + Castro criminal complaint + Lyons 'untruthful statements' + Rosen dismissal-with-prejudice + Bovino personnel removal without retraction. The load-bearing finding: the cumulative-count pattern is named by three independent layers (Reuters review, Hennepin County criminal complaint, federal perjury probe), the named-state-level prosecution (Moriarty/Castro) is the first in the pattern, and the named-federal-perjury-probe (Lyons) is the legal mechanism that converts the narrative pattern into specific consequence with a termination-or-criminal-prosecution ladder. The structural inversion: the on-record DHS framing preceded the video evidence in each case, but the video evidence persisted in the public record while the framing remained online — the silence-as-evidence layer is the unretracted statements. The DHS press release containing 'dozens of false statements' that 'remains online' is the asymmetry.
